policy.selectors: Compiler-owned artifacts derived from named Elements and semantic conditions; never authored as raw selectors.
policy.atRules: Compiler-owned artifacts derived from semantic declarations; never authored as raw at-rules.
policy.aliases: Unsupported redundant spellings; use the mapped canonical capability.
policy.shorthands: Unsupported redundant spellings; structured semantic fields lower to canonical longhands.
policy.standards: Standards entries are gap-detection inputs grouped into product outcomes; they are not a public vocabulary or a property-by-property implementation backlog.

currentCapabilities.gap: Reusable named areas, fragmentation, and advanced positioning are not covered.
Specialized display-environment conditions are not covered.
Advanced typography, masks, compositing, motion paths, and 3D are not covered.
Rotated ancestry and the broader text/layout continuity corpus remain open.
Difficult browser fixtures and calibrated performance budgets remain open.
Accessibility semantics and interaction behavior belong to Platform structure and Components.
Navigation, data, and external effects belong to Programs and Dependencies.
Retained GPU scenes and native controls require another UI-capable Platform and adapter.
Print conditions, paged-media layout, and page presentation have no semantic path.
Meaningful text and accessibility content belong to structure; adapter-owned decoration does not justify a second content path.
Typed anchor relationships and fallback placement have no semantic layout path.
Existing observations and temporal values express the outcome, but native timeline optimization and compatibility evidence remain open.

standardsOutcomes.gap: Syntax, cascade, custom-property, namespace, and authoring-macro standards are compiler or artifact mechanisms rather than additional public Presentation vocabulary.
Current typed values cover the existing language, while broader math, intrinsic-size, environment, and interpolation value outcomes require outcome fixtures before semantic expansion.

Container size and shape, container-relative lengths, selected environment conditions, typed boolean composition, and typed ancestor-state derivation work; specialized display environments remain open.

Logical flow, flex, grid line/span placement, subgrid, overlays, sizing, snapping scroll collections, scrollbar presentation, and continuity work; reusable named areas, anchors, fragmentation, multicolumn, and shapes remain open. Touch policy and virtualization are delegated to Component behavior.

Core application typography, bounded multi-line text, and vertical block flow work; variable-font controls, bidirectional language structure, ruby, counters, text emphasis, advanced decoration, and metric overrides remain open or require delegation fixtures.
Current colors, surfaces, borders, shadows, effects, images, and typed assets work; masks, compositing, advanced gradients, vector paint, and color-management outcomes remain open.

Deterministic temporal values, interruption, and layout continuity work; motion paths, scroll and view timelines, pointer timelines, view transitions, and advanced 3D outcomes remain unclassified or incomplete.

Presentation can respond to exposed interaction state, but selector families must be split between visual state, Component behavior, accessibility structure, and specialized controls without importing raw selectors.
Print and paged-media Presentation remain missing. Meaningful generated content is delegated to structure so accessibility and document meaning do not diverge.

Timed text, responsive source selection, link parameters, and immersive overlay outcomes belong primarily to structure, media Components, or specialized adapters unless a visual-only gap is demonstrated.
